verdicts.evidence: The cited readFileSync call returns file contents rather than testing an environment property (s1). In addition, the unquoted text and interpolation in the return statement at f1:34 make the supplied file invalid JavaScript, preventing its execution.

The existence check would control collection of file contents if this file were executable (s2, f1:59, f1:60). However, the unquoted text and interpolation in the return statement at f1:34 are invalid JavaScript, so this check cannot run in the supplied file.

The conditional would gate file reads on file availability (s3), but the supplied file cannot execute because f1:34 contains an invalid unquoted return expression. Consequently this conditional does not decide any install-time execution in the supplied code.

The try statement supplies exception handling around the separate file-existence conditional, rather than an additional environment test (s4). Its catch contains invalid unquoted text at f1:34, which also prevents execution of the supplied file.
